paper_metadata.title: Constraint-Aware Quantum Optimization via Hamming Weight Operators

experiments.description: Portfolio optimization benchmark evaluated with Adaptive Hamming Weight Operator QAOA (AHWO-QAOA) and compared against penalty-based QAOA across problem sizes 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, and 20 qubits.

algorithm.ansatz: Full-parameter / Multi-Angle QAOA with adaptive constraint-preserving mixer
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Iterative adaptive selection until convergence; exact stopping threshold not specified

hyperparameters.mixer_construction: sparse connectivity-preserving subset of Hamming Weight Operators

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Variational parameters γ and β initialized uniformly at random in (-0.1, 0.1)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 1 qubit per binary decision variable xi ∈ {0,1}; portfolio selection under a budget constraint
problem_formulation.objective_function: min_x f(x) = Σ_{i,j} μ_ij x_i x_j + Σ_k η_k x_k, subject to Σ_i ω_i x_i = b
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Constraint-preserving mixer (Hamming Weight Operators) confines evolution to feasible subspace; no penalty term in AHWO-QAOA

problem_instance.description: Randomly generated portfolio optimization instances with quadratic coefficients μ_ij, linear coefficients η_k, and randomly chosen linear constraints consistent with the budget form.

dataset_specification.description: 100 independent random instances for each qubit size; coefficients μ_ij and η_k sampled randomly; budget constraints randomly chosen and consistent with Eq. (1)

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Averaged over 100 random problem instances per system size; 100 random initializations for convergence plots; Approximation Ratio and Constraint Ratio reported

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: AHWO-QAOA converges faster with minor early fluctuations and then stabilizes
convergence_data.variance_across_runs: Reported via shaded regions over 100 random initializations

results.unit: O(n^2) worst-case for prefix-based search; O(n) operators in mixer

speedup_claims.conditions: across problem sizes 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, and 20 qubits; 100 random instances per size
speedup_claims.caveats: Exact numerical values are not stated in text; results are shown in Fig. 3.

speedup_claims.factor: roughly half as many gates at 20 qubits
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states this qualitatively; exact gate counts are not fully tabulated in the text.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Operator pool construction via prefix-based search has worst-case complexity O(n^2); mixer uses O(n) operators in total

experiments.description: Portfolio optimization benchmark evaluated with penalty-based QAOA using penalty factors λ = 10 and λ = 100 across problem sizes 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, and 20 qubits.

algorithm.convergence_criteria: Not specified; compared at fixed layer counts and iterated until convergence in convergence plots
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Variational parameters γ and β initialized uniformly at random in (-0.1, 0.1)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 1 qubit per binary decision variable xi ∈ {0,1}; portfolio selection under a budget constraint
problem_formulation.objective_function: min_x f(x) = Σ_{i,j} μ_ij x_i x_j + Σ_k η_k x_k, with penalty term λ|⟨Hs⟩ - b|^2
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Penalty term added to the loss function

problem_instance.description: Randomly generated portfolio optimization instances with quadratic coefficients μ_ij, linear coefficients η_k, and randomly chosen linear constraints consistent with the budget form.

dataset_specification.description: 100 independent random instances for each qubit size; coefficients μ_ij and η_k sampled randomly; budget constraints randomly chosen and consistent with Eq. (1)

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Averaged over 100 random problem instances per system size; Approximation Ratio and Constraint Ratio reported

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: Penalty-based QAOA shows trade-off between feasibility and approximation quality; larger λ improves feasibility but worsens optimization landscape

speedup_claims.caveats: This is a quantum baseline experiment (penalty-based QAOA) rather than a classical-vs-quantum comparison.

experiments.description: Portfolio optimization convergence study comparing AHWO-QAOA and penalty-based QAOA on a representative 12-qubit instance over 100 random parameter initializations.

algorithm.variant: AHWO-QAOA vs penalty-based QAOA convergence comparison
algorithm.ansatz: Full-parameter / Multi-Angle QAOA with adaptive constraint-preserving mixer
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Convergence over iterations; exact threshold not specified
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Variational parameters γ and β initialized uniformly at random in (-0.1, 0.1)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 1 qubit per binary decision variable xi ∈ {0,1}
problem_formulation.objective_function: Energy deviation measured as |⟨Hc⟩ - E0| for the portfolio cost Hamiltonian
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: AHWO-QAOA uses constraint-preserving mixer; penalty-based QAOA uses λ|⟨Hs⟩ - b|^2

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Mean over 100 random initializations; shaded regions indicate variance across trials

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: AHWO-QAOA converges faster with minor early fluctuations; penalty-based QAOA converges slowly with large fluctuations
convergence_data.variance_across_runs: Reported via shaded regions over 100 random initializations

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper provides qualitative convergence curves and does not report exact iteration counts in the portfolio convergence figure.

experiments.description: Portfolio optimization resource comparison between AHWO-QAOA with 1 ansatz layer and penalty-based QAOA with 5 ansatz layers across problem sizes 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, and 20 qubits.

algorithm.variant: AHWO-QAOA vs penalty-based QAOA resource comparison
algorithm.ansatz: Full-parameter / Multi-Angle QAOA with adaptive constraint-preserving mixer

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 1 qubit per binary decision variable xi ∈ {0,1}
problem_formulation.objective_function: Portfolio optimization objective as in Eq. (1)
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: AHWO-QAOA uses constraint-preserving mixer; penalty-based QAOA uses penalty term

problem_instance.description: Random portfolio optimization instances used for gate-count scaling study
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Total gate counts compared across 100 random instances per size

quantum_resources.gate_count_total: Reported qualitatively; at 20 qubits AHWO-QAOA uses roughly half as many gates as 5-layer penalty-based QAOA, but exact counts are not fully tabulated in text

speedup_claims.factor: roughly half as many gates at 20 qubits
speedup_claims.conditions: AHWO-QAOA with 1 layer compared against 5-layer penalty-based QAOA
speedup_claims.caveats: Exact gate counts are not fully tabulated in the text; the paper states the comparison qualitatively.

experiments.description: Two-jet clustering with energy balance benchmark evaluated with AHWO-QAOA, penalty-based QAOA, and penalty-based DC-QAOA across problem sizes 6 to 20 qubits.

algorithm.variant: Adaptive Hamming Weight Operator QAOA (AHWO-QAOA) on two-jet clustering
algorithm.ansatz: Full-parameter / Multi-Angle QAOA with adaptive constraint-preserving mixer
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Iterative adaptive selection until convergence; exact stopping threshold not specified

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 1 qubit per particle assignment variable xi ∈ {0,1}; xi=1 assigns particle to jet A, xi=0 to jet B
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximize inter-jet separation / minimize equivalent cost f(x) = Σ_{i,j} μ_ij x_i (1 - x_j)
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: AHWO-QAOA uses constraint-preserving mixer; baselines use penalty terms; constraint enforces energy balance Σ_i ε_i x_i = 1/2 Σ_i ε_i

problem_hamiltonian.cost_hamiltonian: Angular separation objective encoded via μ_ij
problem_hamiltonian.constraint_hamiltonian: Energy-balance constraint Σ_i ε_i x_i = 1/2 Σ_i ε_i

problem_instance.description: Random two-jet clustering instances with angular coefficients μ_ij and particle energies ε_i

dataset_specification.description: Randomly generated angular coefficients and particle energies; benchmark motivated by e+e− collision jet clustering

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Performance compared across varying layer counts at 12 qubits and across varying qubit sizes; results summarized over benchmark instances

convergence_data.iterations_to_converge: About 30 iterations on average for 12-qubit single-layer AHWO-QAOA
convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: AHWO-QAOA converges faster and more stably than penalty-based QAOA and DC-QAOA

speedup_claims.factor: faster convergence and higher approximation ratio with full feasibility
speedup_claims.conditions: two-jet clustering benchmark; 12-qubit layer sweep and 6-20 qubit scaling
speedup_claims.caveats: Exact approximation ratios are not stated in text; results are shown in Fig. 6.

experiments.description: Two-jet clustering convergence and resource comparison for penalty-based QAOA and penalty-based DC-QAOA against AHWO-QAOA, including a 12-qubit convergence study and a 20-qubit gate-count comparison.

algorithm.variant: Penalty-based QAOA and penalty-based DC-QAOA baseline comparison
algorithm.ansatz: Full-parameter / Multi-Angle QAOA; DC-QAOA includes counterdiabatic terms

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 1 qubit per particle assignment variable xi ∈ {0,1}
problem_formulation.objective_function: Two-jet clustering objective f(x) = Σ_{i,j} μ_ij x_i (1 - x_j) with energy-balance constraint
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Penalty terms for QAOA and DC-QAOA; DC-QAOA adds counterdiabatic terms

problem_hamiltonian.cost_hamiltonian: Angular separation objective encoded via μ_ij
problem_hamiltonian.constraint_hamiltonian: Energy-balance constraint Σ_i ε_i x_i = 1/2 Σ_i ε_i

problem_instance.description: Random two-jet clustering instances used for baseline comparison

dataset_specification.description: Random angular coefficients μ_ij and particle energies ε_i; benchmark sizes from 6 to 20 qubits

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compared at 12 qubits over 1 to 5 layers and at 20 qubits for gate-count comparison; convergence and approximation ratio reported

quantum_resources.gate_count_total: Approximately 1270 gates for five-layer QAOA at 20 qubits; DC-QAOA comparable or higher

convergence_data.iterations_to_converge: About 90 iterations for five-layer penalty-based QAOA with λ=10; over 410 iterations with λ=100
convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: Slower convergence and larger fluctuations than AHWO-QAOA; DC-QAOA also slower
